title: The curse on the House of Atreus
lead: Five generations, each paying for the last.

steps.text: Tantalus serves his son Pelops to the gods. The gods restore the boy; Tantalus is punished forever.
Pelops wins Hippodamia by bribing Myrtilus, then throws him into the sea. Falling, Myrtilus curses Pelops and all his line.
Thyestes seduces his brother’s wife and steals the golden lamb. Atreus feeds Thyestes his own sons, and Thyestes curses the house of Atreus.
Agamemnon sacrifices Iphigenia to sail for Troy. On his return, Clytemnestra and Aegisthus kill him.
Orestes kills his mother and Aegisthus. Hunted by the Furies, he is tried in Athens and acquitted. The chain breaks.

title: The curse on the House of Labdacus
lead: A crime in Pelops’s house echoes through Thebes.

steps.text: Laius abducts Chrysippus, the son of Pelops, and Pelops curses him. Only later sources tell this origin.
An oracle warns Laius that his son will kill him. He has the infant exposed on a mountain.
Grown and unaware, Oedipus kills Laius at a crossroads and marries the widowed queen, his mother. When the truth comes out, Jocasta dies and Oedipus blinds himself.
Oedipus curses his sons, and they kill each other over Thebes. Antigone buries Polynices against the king’s order and is condemned.
